35.0.0.en: 1 He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough. 2 He that taketh heed to the commandments hath sacrificed a peace offering. 3 And he that departeth from iniquity hath sacrificed a sin offering, and hath made atonement for his sins. 4 He that offereth fine flour hath paid his thanks, and he that giveth alms hath sacrificed a sacrifice of praise. 5 To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to the Lord, and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation for sins. 6 Thou shalt not appear empty before the Lord; 7 for all these things are done because of the commandment. 8 The offering of the righteous maketh the altar fat, and the sweet savour thereof is before the most High. 9 The sacrifice of a just man is acceptable, and the memorial thereof shall never be forgotten. 10 Give the Lord his honour with a good eye, and diminish not the firstfruits of thine hands. 11 In all thy gifts shew a cheerful countenance, and dedicate thy tithes with gladness. 12 Give unto the most High according as he hath given, and offer the gain of thine hand with a good eye. 13 For the Lord recompenseth, and will recompense thee seven times as much.

35.0.1.en: The Book of Leviticus, which is considered the book of the call to holiness, since the saying is repeated: "Ye shall be holy unto me: for I am holy" (Lev 11:44; 11:45; 19:2), was concerned to speak in some detail about sacrifices and offerings in the temple of God. And the Book of Ben Sirach came to call every believer to offer spiritual sacrifices and offerings in his life. So he saw that he who keeps the commandments offers a peace offering [1], and he who does a kindness to one in need offers an offering of fine flour [2], and he who gives alms sacrifices a thank offering to God [2]. And he who withdraws from evil offers a sin offering with which God is pleased [2]. He links the service of the temple with the believers' offering of sacrifices and offerings in their daily life in the presence of the Lord.

35.0.2.en: The man who keeps the Law multiplies his offerings, and he who holds fast to the commandments offers a peace offering [1].

35.0.3.en: God is pleased with offerings of obedience to the divine commandment and holding fast to it, and counts them offerings and a peace offering pleasing before Him. The peace offering, in the view of Origen, is the offering of the spiritually mature or perfect man who enjoys the perfect peace of God in his inner life and in his inner relationships, as an overflow of peace and thanksgiving springing forth in the Lord Christ Himself, the giver of peace.

35.0.4.en: v True peace is from above. As long as we are bound to the body, we bear a yoke of many things that weary us.

35.0.5.en: Seek peace, then, and be freed from the troubles of this world. Acquire a quiet mind, and a calm, unperturbed soul, which passions do not stir up, and false teachings do not attract, so that it defies their allurements to accept them, that you may obtain "the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts" (Phil 4:7).

35.0.6.en: He who seeks peace seeks Christ, for He Himself is our peace, who maketh the twain one new man (Eph 14:2), making peace through the blood of His cross, whether things in earth, or things in heaven [1].

35.1.0.en: St. Basil the Great He who requites with kindness offers an offering of fine flour, and he who gives alms offers a sacrifice of thanksgiving [2].

35.1.1.en: Origen says: if you are unable to offer your whole life consecrated to the Lord as a burnt offering (Lev 1), then offer your daily work, sanctified to Him, as an offering of flour or unleavened bread, crying out to God to pour into you the oil of His mercy without ceasing, that the world may not distract you from your eternity (Lev 2). And he who gives alms is like one who sacrifices a sacrifice of thanksgiving.

35.1.2.en: v When you lie down on your bed, remember the blessings of God and His care for you, and thank Him for this; for as you are filled with these thoughts you rejoice in the Spirit. Then in the sleep of the body there will be an elevation for your soul, and the closing of your eyes will be a true knowledge of God, and your silence, while you are charged with good feelings, is a glorification of Almighty God with all the heart and all the strength, offering to God a praise that rises to the heights. For when there is no evil in a man, thanksgiving alone pleases God more than costly offerings, to Him who is the glory forever and ever. Amen [2].

35.1.3.en: St. Anthony the Great v Question: How can a man fulfil his love to God?

35.2.0.en: Answer: When we are in a state of continual thanksgiving and gratitude for the graces of God... as we see it also with irrational animals. Dogs, for example, love those who offer them food. We also learn this principle from the Lord's accusation of the people of Israel by the tongue of the prophet Isaiah, saying: "I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me. The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master's crib: but Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider" (Isa 1:2-3). As love grows spontaneously in the ass toward its master, and the ox toward its owner, so also we. If we thank God gratefully for His graces that He gives us, how then shall we not love Him who grants us so many of those great gifts?! How is such a virtue not formed in the conscience of the sound soul naturally, without learning it (practicing it), so to speak?! [3]

35.2.1.en: St. Basil the Great To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to the Lord, and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation [3].

35.2.2.en: Some peoples became acquainted, through tradition, with bloody sacrifices, having received them from Noah and his three sons, but they distorted their concepts and purpose. But the Jewish people alone had the rite of "the great Day of Atonement" (Lev 16), the like of which one seeks in vain among any other people, and it points to the sacrifice of the Cross which the Lord Christ offered for the world. "Atonement" in Hebrew, "kebodit," means "covering" or "concealing," for on this day sins are forgiven and the man is covered by the precious blood, and the high priest makes atonement for himself and for the priests and for all the congregation, and even for the tabernacle and all its contents, a general and collective atonement for that into which the congregation as a whole, or as members, had fallen throughout the year.

35.2.3.en: Ben Sirach sees that departing from evil is the offering of atonement.

35.3.0.en: You shall not appear before the Lord empty-handed, for all these offerings are offered because of the commandment [4].

35.3.1.en: The commandment was often repeated: "None shall appear before me empty" (Ex 34:20), since the temple was committed to helping the needy, and also gave the priests and Levites portions of what was offered to the altar for their living and their families'. So it befits the believer not to appear empty. St. Mary, in her visit to Elizabeth her kinswoman, did not bring gifts in kind on the occasion of Elizabeth's pregnancy, but entered bearing the Lord Christ incarnate in her womb, and the babe leaped in her womb and Elizabeth rejoiced, saying: "And whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?" (Lk 1:43). So it befits us to follow St. Mary's example and not appear empty, but to bring to our brethren the Lord Christ dwelling in our hearts, He "in whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge" (Col 3:3). And when we stand in the presence of the Father we have nothing to offer except Christ our righteousness (1 Cor 1:30).

35.4.0.en: The righteous and good offering is anointing oil for the altar, and its sweet savour rises up before the Most High [5].

35.4.1.en: The Apostle says: "Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?" (1 Cor 3:16). If we are the temple of God, the inner altar in our hearts must be anointed with the anointing of the righteousness of Christ, and the incense of pure prayers be offered upon it, sending forth the sweet savour of Christ (2 Cor 2:15). Thus he links the ecclesiastical rite with the holy life.

35.5.0.en: The sacrifice of the righteous is acceptable, and the memorial of it shall never be forgotten [6].

35.5.1.en: The goal of our worship and our communion with the Holy One is that we become holy, bearing the icon of our God. For He has no need of offerings, but that we bear His righteousness and be prepared for eternal glory. His delight is not in the multitude of offerings but in the purity of our hearts, which will be revealed on the great Day of the Lord, and we shall enjoy the fellowship of the eternal glories. The Apostle repeats the saying: "The just shall live by faith" (Rom 1:17; Gal 3:11; Heb 10:38).

35.6.0.en: Glorify the Lord with your generosity, and do not be sparing of the firstfruits of your hands [7].

35.6.1.en: Generosity in offering reveals the righteousness of God working in us, and our pride in the glory of the Lord. It is not fitting for the believer to be sparing with the firstfruits and tithes, but to bring them with joy. "He which soweth sparingly shall reap also sparingly; and he which soweth bountifully shall reap also bountifully. Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver (1 Cor 9:7).

35.7.0.en: In every gift be of a cheerful countenance, and dedicate your tithes with gladness [8].

35.7.1.en: St. Irenaeus says: "Judah dedicated the tithes of their incomes to God, but as for those who have received freedom (in Christ), they place all that they have at the disposal of Christ."

35.7.2.en: Give to the Most High as He has given you; give to Him generously according to your own unexpected gain[4] [9].

35.7.3.en: The prophet Malachi gives us sincere advice, in the words of the Lord, that we may touch practically how giving generously opens before us the windows of heaven, so that divine gifts flow upon us from where we do not expect. "Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in mine house, and prove me now herewith, saith the LORD of hosts, if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there shall not be room enough to receive it" (Mal 3:10).

35.8.0.en: For the Lord is the one who rewards; He will reward you sevenfold [10].

35.8.1.en: The Lord rewards the one who is generous in giving materially, and gives him inner joy and spiritual blessings.

35.9.s.en: 2. There is no partiality with God

35.9.0.en: 14 Offer not gifts that have a blemish, for the Lord will not receive them. 15 And trust not in an unrighteous sacrifice; for the Lord is judge, and with him is no respect of persons. 16 He will not accept persons against the poor, but will hear the prayer of the oppressed. 17 He will not despise the fatherless that supplicateth him, nor the widow, when she poureth out her complaint. 18 Do not the tears of the widow run down her cheeks? and is not her cry against him that causeth them to fall? 19 For from her cheeks they go up to heaven, and the Lord that heareth will not delight in them. 20 He that serveth is accepted with good-will, and his prayer reacheth unto the clouds. 21 The prayer of the humble pierceth the clouds, and it will not rest till it come nigh, and will not depart till the most High shall visit and judge righteously and execute judgment. 22 For the Lord will not be slack, neither will he be long patient toward them, till he have smitten in sunder the loins of the unmerciful; 23 and avenged himself on the heathen, till he have taken away the multitude of the proud, and broken the sceptres of the unrighteous. 24 Till he have rendered to every man according to his deeds, and to the works of men according to their intents. 25 Till he have judged the cause of his people, and made them to rejoice in his mercy. 26 Mercy is seasonable in the time of affliction, as clouds of rain in the time of drought.

35.9.1.en: Do not offer Him a bribe, for He does not accept it, and do not offer a sacrifice of injustice [11].

35.9.2.en: The Lord Christ says: "I am the way, the truth" (Jn 14:6). And St. John the Beloved says: "God is love" (1 Jn 4:8, 16). So He does not accept a bribe from one who ignores the truth, and from one who does not practice love but injustice, and He does not show partiality. What is the connection of acceptable worship with bribery? Some think that by their contributing to houses of worship or by giving alms they obtain forgiveness of their sins without repentance and returning to God, as though they were bribing God.

35.9.3.en: For the Lord is the Judge, and with Him there is no partiality [12].

35.9.4.en: The Lord is as a father to the orphans, and as a judge to the widows, a defender of the oppressed, and a shepherd to the needy and suffering; He does not show partiality to the rich who have no pity on their brethren. He is no respecter of persons (Deut 10:17; Job 34:19).

35.9.5.en: He does not show partiality at the expense of the poor, but hears the petition of the oppressed [13].

35.9.6.en: There is no partiality with God (Rom 2:11); He cares for the poor and needy and oppressed, but He does not give to the person unwilling to work and the lazy, nor does He support one who counts himself wronged if it is because of his neglect and slackness.

35.9.7.en: He does not neglect the supplication of the orphan, nor that of the widow when she pours out her complaint [14].

35.10.0.en: Do not the widow's tears run down her cheeks, and does she not cry out against him who caused them? [15].

35.10.1.en: Here he highlighted God's concern for the care of the oppressed classes. His ears listen to the supplications of orphans and widows, and to their tears and cries.

35.11.0.en: He whose service pleases the Lord will be accepted by Him, and his prayer reaches the clouds [16].

35.11.1.en: Because Moses served the Lord faithfully, the Lord answered the cries of his heart before he cried with his mouth (Ex 14:15). Origen said: [God hears the silent cries of the saints by the Holy Spirit.]

35.12.0.en: The prayer of the humble man pierces the clouds, and he does not rest until it reaches the Lord [17].

35.12.1.en: The humble man perceives that his prayer has reached God not only through visible or tangible signs, but, what is more important, he feels a true inner rest; he feels that he is in the bosom of God.

35.12.2.en: v Remember the pure conscience (of Job) and his blameless prayer: "O earth, cover not the blood of my body" (Job 16:18) LXX, that his prayer might go up as incense toward the Lord (Ps 141:2), and not be deposited in the earth.

35.12.3.en: The prayer of the saint pierces the cloud (cf. Sir 35:17), but the earth opens her mouth, and hides the prayer of the sinner in the blood of the flesh, as God said to Cain the murderer: "Cursed art thou from the earth, which hath opened her mouth to receive thy brother's blood from thy hand, as long as thou art earth" (cf. Gen 4:11-12) [5].

35.12.4.en: St. Ambrose v Let us now come to silent prayer, the prayer of Hannah the mother of Samuel. How she became an object of God's pleasure, and opened her barren womb, and removed her reproach, and bore a Nazirite or priest (1 Sam 1).

35.12.5.en: And Samuel also, when he prayed before his God and showed the wickedness of the Israelites when they asked for a king. Samuel offered a whole sacrifice upon the altar (1 Sam 12:17-18), and the rain came down...

35.12.6.en: David also prayed before his God and was delivered from the hands of Saul. And he also prayed after he had numbered the people and turned away from them the divine wrath and punishment when the destroyer had gained authority over them (2 Sam 24:17).

35.12.7.en: Asa also prayed, and his prayer showed great power, when Zerah the Ethiopian came out against him with an army of a million. Then Asa prayed and said: "Your power will be known, O our God, when You destroy a huge people by a few people" (2 Chr 14:12-15). So this great army was defeated by the power of Asa's prayer.

35.12.8.en: His son Jehoshaphat shattered the enemy's army by his prayer, which defeated them (2 Chr 20:3-30).

35.12.9.en: Hezekiah also prayed, and by his prayer he prevailed over 185,000 men, the angel acting as the leader of his army (2 Kgs 19:15, 35).

35.12.10.en: Jonah prayed before his God from the depths of the sea and God heard him (Jon 2), and answered his prayer, and he was delivered without any harm. His prayer pierced the depths, and overcame the waves, and was stronger than the storm. It pierced the clouds and flew in the air (cf. Sir 35:17), it opened the heavens and drew near to the throne of majesty by means of Gabriel who presents prayer before God. As a result the depths cast out the prophet, and the whale brought Jonah safely to the land. Likewise in the case of Hananiah, Azariah and Mishael, their prayers overcame the flame, and quenched the power of the fire, and changed its burning nature. They put out the king's fury, and delivered the righteous men (Dan 3)..

35.12.11.en: When Daniel also prayed, his prayer shut the mouths of the lions (Dan 6); the devouring mouths were shut before the flesh and bones of a man. The lions spread their paws, and caught Daniel so that he would not fall to the ground, embraced him in their arms, and kissed his feet. And when Daniel stood in the pit to pray, he lifted his hands to heaven, and after the pattern of Daniel the lions followed him and imitated him. That One who received his prayer came down and shut the mouths of the lions. For Daniel said to Darius: "My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths, that they have not hurt me" (Dan 6:22).

35.12.12.en: And although the pit was covered and sealed, light shone inside it, and the lions rejoiced when they saw the light that appeared for the sake of Daniel. And when sleep overcame Daniel and he wished to doze, the lions knelt that he might sleep upon them, and not on the ground. The pit was more illuminated than an upper chamber with many windows. And in the pit he offered many prayers more than in his upper chamber, where he used to pray only three times a day (Dan 6:10), and when Daniel triumphed and rejoiced, those who had accused him were thrown into the pit instead of him, and the mouths of the lions opened and devoured them and crushed their bones [6].

35.12.13.en: St. Aphrahat v Above all this, let him observe the words of the Apostle: "For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us" (Rom 8:18), and expect the revelation with David: "in keeping of them there is great reward" (Ps 19:12), and recompense and crowns of righteousness, and the eternal dwelling, and the life without end, and the unspeakable joy, and the unperishing places with the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, who is the true God in heaven, and the meeting face to face, and rejoicing with the angels and fathers and patriarchs and prophets and apostles and martyrs, that we may be numbered with these, by the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, to whom belong power and glory forever and ever. Amen.

35.13.0.en: St. Basil the Great And he will not withdraw it until the Most High visits him, and does justice to the righteous, and executes judgment [18].

35.13.1.en: v Here we overcome the adversary, if we fight with tears and prayers and a broken heart continually. It is written: "The prayer of the humble pierces the clouds ... and does not cease until the Most High visits him." Therefore the weeping of the humble contributes with great power to the destruction of fleshly lust. Tears issuing from the pricking of the heart defeat the enemy and acquire on our behalf the gift of triumphant happiness [7].

35.13.2.en: Fr. Fulgentius v In ancient times six hundred thousand armed men of the children of Israel went forward against Midian, and all of them were defeated because of the sin lurking in them (Num 11:21). Now the Midianites, victors over six hundred thousand, were struck down by two thousand, that you may know that Israel was not victorious because of the large number of soldiers, but by the righteousness and godliness in which they are.

35.13.3.en: And in blessing them it was said that if they kept the law of the Lord, one of them would defeat a thousand, and two would put ten thousand to flight (Lev 26:8). Behold then, one saint praying is better than countless sinners in battle. The prayer of the saint pierces heaven (the clouds) [17], how then should it not defeat earthly enemies? For this reason it befits you in every way to labor, first to seek and to keep the righteousness of God (Mt 6:33).

35.13.4.en: If you obtain (the righteousness of God) and keep it, He will subdue all your enemies to you. If the Apostle says: "Having on the breastplate of righteousness, and your loins girt about with truth, and the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit ... Above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked" (cf. Eph 6:14-17). When you are armed with these weapons you are able to fight all the camps of Satan and all his army, and sing with assurance: "Though an host should encamp against me, my heart shall not fear: though war should rise against me, in this will I be confident" (Ps 27:2) [8].

35.14.0.en: Origen For the Lord will not delay, nor be slow in helping them [19].

35.15.0.en: Until He crushes the loins of those without mercy, and repays with vengeance upon the nations [20]

35.16.0.en: Until He wipes out the multitudes of the proud, and breaks the scepter of the unrighteous [21].

35.16.1.en: With many words the Pharisee offered a haughty prayer, while with few words the tax collector offered a humble prayer. The first was rejected, and the second passed through to the throne of God, for God listens to the words of the humble.

35.16.2.en: v It is fitting that our petitions be offered to God in humility, for it is our heart that is heard, not our voice. God, who sees our thoughts, is not to be petitioned by shouting, as the Lord affirms when He says: "Wherefore think ye ... in your hearts?" (Mt 9:4). And in another place: "And all the churches shall know that I am he which searcheth the reins and hearts" (cf. Rev 2:23) [9].

35.17.0.en: The martyr Cyprian Until He renders to man according to his deeds, and to the works of men according to their thoughts [22].

35.17.1.en: The heavenly life that we live here is a pledge of the immortal life extending beyond the limits of time, when the Lord Christ the King appears with His angels to recompense each one according to his work. If faith is the foundation of the Kingdom, it must nevertheless be "practical," so that the Lord may give us the eternal crowns, recompensing "each one according to his work."

35.18.0.en: Until He executes judgment for His people, and makes them rejoice in His mercy [23].

35.18.1.en: St. John Chrysostom sees that Moses, with all the esteem he had reached in the eyes of God, cannot grasp the depths of God's wisdom and mercy, as though God were saying to him: [O Moses, it is not for you to know who is worthy of My love for man; leave this to Me. If it is not Moses' right to know, how much more is it so for us?[10]]

35.18.2.en: Mercy is beautiful in the time of his affliction[11], like rain in the time of drought [24].

35.18.3.en: While the Lord of glory suffered bodily the sufferings of the Cross, He offered to mankind His mercy, and made atonement for their sins. St. Augustine also says that afflictions bring us into contact with the mercy of God and His care and love.

35.18.4.en: v "Hear me, O LORD, for thy mercy is sweet" (Ps 69:16).. For the man who is in troubles, he needs to find sweetness in the mercies of God. Concerning this sweetness of God's mercies see what is said in another place, where Holy Scripture says: "Mercy is seasonable in the time of affliction, as clouds of rain in the time of drought" (cf. Sir 35:24)... Even bread is not sweet unless hunger precedes it. For this reason, even when God permits or wills that we be in any affliction, even in this He is merciful. He will not withdraw help, but stirs up in us the longing (for Him) [12].

35.18.5.en: v "In the daytime the LORD will command his mercy, and in the night He will declare it" (cf. Ps 42:8). In affliction a man has no leisure to hear. Listen when you are at ease. Learn, when you are in quiet, the discipline of wisdom, and store up the word of God as you do with food. For in the time of distress it befits everyone to benefit from what he heard in the time of security. For in the time of ease God commands you His mercy (Ps 42:8), and as you serve Him faithfully, He frees you from distress. Only in the night does He declare to you His mercy which He commanded you in the daytime. When distress actually comes, He will not leave you deprived of His help, but shows you that what He commanded you in the daytime is true. It is written: "Mercy is seasonable in the time of affliction, as clouds of rain in the time of drought" (cf. Sir 35:24) [13].

35.19.s.en: Accept my life as a sacrifice of pleasing love!

35.19.0.en: v You loved me and offered Your life as a sacrifice for my salvation; what shall I render to You, O All-Love!

35.19.1.en: Grant me to keep Your Law, that my heart may be purified.

35.19.2.en: Let me keep Your commandment, and my heart will be filled with holiness and peace.

35.19.3.en: v I see You before me in my brethren, so I walk with them in kindness and generosity.

35.19.4.en: By Your grace I flee from evil, and enjoy Your righteousness.

35.19.5.en: I have nothing to offer You, for all that I offer is from You.

35.19.6.en: Set up for Yourself an altar within me, and anoint it with the oil of gladness.

35.19.7.en: I offer upon it my prayers, bearing Your fragrance, O Holy One.

35.19.8.en: That I may possess You and see Your glory, and enjoy Your sweet voice!

35.19.9.en: v You have no need of my worship and my goodness. Grant me compassion for the poor, and a longing to remove injustice, and a desire to free the captives and prisoners, and to heal the sick.

35.19.10.en: You are the Father of orphans, the Judge of widows, O God of the forgotten!

35.19.11.en: v You are pleased with the prayer of the heart; You alone hear it, and are pleased with it, and answer its cries.

35.19.12.en: And there is no enemy who can obstruct it.

35.19.13.en: What shall I ask of You, O Giver of good things?

35.19.14.en: Give my prayer the two wings of the Spirit, that it may fly and pierce the clouds.

35.19.15.en: It will rest in Your bosom, You will grant me Your free righteousness, and gather me into Your heavenly house!

35.19.16.en: My God, my heart asks You to hasten Your coming!
